title: EW Wireless RF Dropouts / Static
shortDescription: Audio cuts in and out on Sennheiser EW wireless mic system.
fullDescription:
Sennheiser EW (Evolution Wireless) systems use UHF bands. Dropouts occur when transmitter and receiver lose line-of-sight, batteries weaken, or another transmitter operates on the same frequency.

In the US, the 600 MHz band reallocation also affects older EW G2/G3 systems.

fixSteps.title: Auto-scan
fixSteps.instruction: On receiver, run Easy Setup / Auto Scan to find clear frequency, then sync TX via IR.

fixSteps.title: Fresh batteries
fixSteps.instruction: Use new alkaline AA or freshly charged BA 2015 packs.

fixSteps.title: Antenna placement
fixSteps.instruction: Mount receiver antennas in a V at ear height with line-of-sight.

whenToCallPro: If multiple channels need coordinating with site survey software.

faq.a: In the US, no — 617-652 MHz is illegal for wireless mics since July 2020.

title: RF Linked but No Audio
shortDescription: EW receiver shows good RF but no AF level when speaking.
fullDescription:
When the receiver shows RF bars but no audio meter activity, the issue is in the audio chain rather than radio. Often the lavalier capsule failed, or the gain (AF Sensitivity) is set too low.

Mute switches on body-pack transmitters are also a common culprit.

fixSteps.title: Unmute
fixSteps.instruction: Set the body-pack mute switch to ON. Verify in MENU -> Mute Mode.

fixSteps.title: Adjust gain
fixSteps.instruction: Increase AF Sensitivity in 6 dB steps until peaks reach -6 dB.

fixSteps.title: Swap capsule
fixSteps.instruction: Try a known good ME 2 / ME 3 / ME 4 capsule.

whenToCallPro: If transmitter audio circuit failed (no audio with multiple known good capsules).

faq.a: No, EW body packs power their own capsules.

title: MD 421 / MD 441 Low Signal
shortDescription: Dynamic mic outputs very low level requiring extreme gain.
fullDescription:
Sennheiser MD-series dynamic microphones (MD 421, MD 441) have moderate sensitivity and need clean preamp gain (60+ dB). When paired with a budget interface, output sounds low.

A bad XLR cable or partly broken voice coil can also drop output further.

fixSteps.title: Use Cloudlifter / Fethead
fixSteps.instruction: Add an inline +25 dB activator between mic and preamp.

faq.a: Will not damage modern Sennheiser dynamics, but does not improve level.

title: ME Condenser Capsule Not Powering
shortDescription: MKE 600 / ME 66 condenser produces no signal.
fullDescription:
Condenser microphones in the Sennheiser ME / MKE shotgun line require either AA battery in the body or 48V phantom power from the mixer. Missing both leaves the mic completely silent.

A bad battery contact or oxidized XLR pin is the common culprit on older units.
symptoms: Hiss when phantom enabled but no signal

fixSteps.title: Insert battery
fixSteps.instruction: Install fresh AA in mic body, observe polarity.

fixSteps.title: Clean contacts
fixSteps.instruction: Use contact cleaner spray on XLR pins and battery springs.

whenToCallPro: If FET inside capsule failed (usually after lightning strike).

title: Body-Pack Low Battery Warning
shortDescription: Transmitter battery indicator flashes red after only minutes of use.
fullDescription:
Body-pack transmitters drop voltage rapidly when the battery is near end of life. Even fresh-looking AAs can show low when the cells are old stock.

NiMH rechargeables (1.2V) trigger low-battery sooner than alkaline (1.5V).

fixSteps.title: Use Lithium AA
fixSteps.instruction: Energizer Ultimate Lithium provides full RF run-time.

fixSteps.title: Battery type setting
fixSteps.instruction: On EW-D set battery type Lithium for accurate metering.

faq.a: Yes for EW-D, gives accurate runtime in minutes.

title: Excessive Plosives on Recording
shortDescription: Loud popping on P and B sounds.
fullDescription:
Plosives are bursts of air hitting the diaphragm. Sennheiser studio condensers (MK 4, e 965) and shotguns (MKH 416) without a pop filter produce loud thumps.

A pop filter or windscreen, plus 4-6 inches distance, eliminates this.

fixSteps.title: Add pop filter
fixSteps.instruction: Mount nylon mesh pop filter 2 inches in front of capsule.

faq.a: Outside yes, indoors a mesh filter is more effective.

title: Constant Buzz on Wireless Mic
shortDescription: Steady 60Hz hum or buzz on wireless mic output.
fullDescription:
A constant buzz on a wireless system is rarely RF. It is usually a ground loop in the receiver-to-mixer audio path, or an unbalanced cable used on the balanced output.

Nearby switching power supplies and dimmers can also induce hum into capsule cabling.

fixSteps.title: Lift ground
fixSteps.instruction: Use an isolation transformer or balanced XLR cable from receiver out.

fixSteps.title: Move phones
fixSteps.instruction: Keep cell phones at least 2 meters from receiver.

whenToCallPro: If you cannot identify the loop with simple swaps.

faq.a: No, never lift the AC ground pin.

title: EW-D Cannot Sync TX to RX
shortDescription: EW-D digital wireless body pack will not link to receiver.
fullDescription:
EW-D systems use digital pairing over Bluetooth Low Energy plus the audio link. If the BLE link fails, pairing aborts. Both units must run matching firmware version.

Running the Smart Assist app while a manual pair is in progress also causes conflicts.

fixSteps.title: Update firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Use Smart Assist app to update both RX and TX to same version.

fixSteps.title: Manual pair
fixSteps.instruction: Hold link button on RX 2 seconds, then on TX, observe link icon.

whenToCallPro: If BLE radio failed in either unit.

title: Heavy Wind Noise on Outdoor Recording
shortDescription: Outdoor recording shows low rumble making audio unusable.
fullDescription:
Even a light breeze creates large excursions on shotgun and lavalier capsules. Without wind protection, recordings have heavy rumble below 200 Hz.

Foam alone is insufficient outdoors; a fur windjammer is required.

fixSteps.title: Use Rycote / fur cover
fixSteps.instruction: Install fur windjammer over foam, sized to mic.

fixSteps.title: Engage HPF
fixSteps.instruction: Activate 100Hz HPF on mic or recorder.

faq.a: No, blocks high frequencies and adds reflection.

title: Wireless Audio Crackles / Distorts
shortDescription: Audio is clear at low volume but distorts when speaker raises voice.
fullDescription:
Distortion on a wireless mic at higher SPL is usually too much input gain on the body-pack — exceeding the AD converter range. Lowering AF Sensitivity in 6-12dB steps usually fixes it.

Digital systems clip hard once over 0 dBFS; analog (EW G4) softer.

fixSteps.title: Reduce AF Sensitivity
fixSteps.instruction: Lower TX AF Sensitivity in -6 dB steps until clean peaks.

fixSteps.title: Match output level
fixSteps.instruction: Set RX output Mic vs Line based on mixer input.

faq.a: EW receivers have a built-in limiter on the output stage.
